title: deal-breakers-and-soft-asks-contract-scratchpad
content:
Quick context:
- Personal scratchpad for upcoming partner NDA + limited pilot SOW. Notes are informal, rough order of priority. Not for external circulation yet.
- Counterparty is a mid-market analytics vendor; they asked to use their master services agreement. We should push back on these main items.

Deal-breakers (blocks without exec/legal approval):
1) Unlimited indemnity for third-party IP claims against Redwood products or services.
   - Why: opens up to unknown exposure; partner likely will try to push all risk onto us.
   - Walk-through ask: carve to "claims arising solely from Partner's gross negligence or willful misconduct" OR mutual IP indemnity.
   - Suggested replacement language (short): "Each party shall indemnify the other for claims arising from the indemnifying party's breach of its representations or gross negligence; neither party shall have obligations to indemnify for indirect or punitive damages."
2) Broad data-use rights that allow partner to retain or train models on any customer data we provide.
   - Why: we need strict restrictions for customer data and telemetry.
   - Ask: explicit prohibition on training models on customer or Redwood-originated data; allowed uses limited to providing the service and agreed analytics.
   - Practical fallback: time-limited, aggregated, deidentified metrics allowed for product improvement, with opt-out.
3) No cap on liability / unlimited consequential liability tied to service interruptions.
   - Ask: Liability cap equal to the fees paid in the prior 12 months (standard) and carve out for gross negligence/fraud. Exclude statutory indemnities but cap otherwise.

Soft asks (nice-to-have; tradeable):
- Shorter security incident notification window: 24 hours initial notice, 72 hours full report. Partner asked for 30 days. Push to 72/7 days for root cause.
- Right to audit / third-party audit SOC2 reports rather than ad-hoc audit clauses. If partner resists, ask for attested reports and annual summary.
- Subprocessor list and change notice: require notification and objection window (10 days) for new subprocessors handling customer data.
- Restrict use of subcontractors in ways that materially affect SLA without prior consent.

Clause-by-clause quick redline cheat sheet (notes to self):
- Termination for convenience: aim for 30 days on either side for pilot SOW. Partner might want 90; push for 30. Document transition assistance obligations (30-60 days).
- SLA / Credits: map availability to concrete credits. If partner's runtime affects our SLA to our customers, require pass-through credits or remediation.
- Confidentiality definition: specifically list "prompt text, customer config, KV cache, model outputs tied to customer" as confidential. Exclude aggregated/anonymous performance metrics.
- IP ownership: ensure customer data and customer-specific prompts/config remain customer's; platform improvements from aggregated metrics can be retained by partner but not traceable back to Redwood customers.
- Export controls & sanctions: standard clause; require partner to notify if their tooling uses re-exported tech that could affect compliance.

Negotiation scripts / talking points (for calls):
- "We can agree to mutual indemnities for IP, but we cannot accept unilateral broad indemnity. Can we make this mutual and limited to proven direct damages?"
- "For training uses, we can permit aggregated and deidentified telemetry for product improvements, but no retention or model training on raw customer content. We can provide a small test dataset for benchmarking if needed under strict controls."
- "We understand you want a long termination notice; for pilots 30 days is industry standard and helps both sides exit quickly if engagement isn't productive."
- "We are open to passing through reasonable audit rights but prefer accepted attestations like SOC2 + reasonable notice for on-site audits."

Fallback positions and escalation matrix (who to loop if counterparty resists):
- If partner refuses liability cap: loop in VP Legal (Miguel) and CFO.
- If partner insists on training rights: escalate to Product (Ava) for business review and to decide whether to accept opt-out terms.
- If partner requests aggressive IP indemnity: require exec signoff; can offer CR-1 (counterparty assumes IP risk for Partner-created integrations only).

Open questions I need to resolve before sending redlines:
- Do we accept a data-processing addendum (DPA) as standalone or embed in MSA? Prefer standalone for reusability.
- Insurance: what minimum limits do we want to require for mid-market partners? (Currently guessing $2M general liability, $5M cyber.) Need to check with insurance broker.
- Are we comfortable with a 12-month liability cap or prefer 6? Pilot fees are small; cap tied to 12 months of fees may be $X which might be low.

Immediate next steps (TODOS):
- Draft redline with the three core carveouts (indemnity, data training ban, liability cap) and circulate to Miguel. (Priority)
- Pull latest SOC2 summary from partner site and attach to redline if available.
- Prepare a one-pager justification for Product on why training on customer data is unacceptable (privacy + model leak risk).
- Schedule 30-min call with partner negotiator; bring Miguel or Ava if clauses are pushed back.

Random notes / negotiation tactics to remember:
- Use "mutuality" as a lever: if they want unilateral rights, ask for a corresponding concession (longer notice, higher SLA credits, or marketing permission).
- Frame training restriction as a narrow business ask: we want to protect customer data, not block partnership. Offer aggregated metrics instead.
- Keep fight for liability cap early; once signed, retro changes are hard.

Draft language snippets I might drop into redline (quick):
- Liability cap: "Except for liability arising from a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, each party's aggregate liability for claims arising out of this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid by Customer to Partner under the SOW in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim."
- Training prohibition: "Partner shall not use Customer Data, including prompts and outputs, to train, fine-tune, or improve machine learning models, except for aggregated and de-identified telemetry for internal product improvement that cannot be reversed or associated with any individual Customer or end user."
- Security incident timing: "Partner will provide (a) initial notification within 24 hours of becoming aware of a Security Incident and (b) a preliminary report within 72 hours, followed by a root cause analysis within 30 days."

End-of-scratchpad notes:
- This doc will become the basis for a tidy redline. Keep this version messy.
- When in doubt, prefer explicit narrow language over vague generalities.
- Follow up: convert into a cleaned redline and upload to Confluence under legal/drafts after signoff.
